messages:
Miles Thornton: Oncall note: we’ve had 3 provisioning runs in the last ~24h get stuck/fail in **Bootstrapping**. All look similar (helm install/upgrade + bootstrap hooks timing out). This is getting noisy + hard to triage quickly.

Miles Thornton: Examples (from #eng-infra and pager notes):
- pool `ded-az1-stg-014` run `prun_01HQR7K8Z2` (correlation `prov-6f3c3b2a`) -> Bootstrapping failed
- pool `ded-az1-stg-015` run `prun_01HQR9P0M4` (correlation `prov-5a11d1f7`) -> Bootstrapping stuck > 45m then Failed
- pool `ded-eu1-stg-006` run `prun_01HQS1A7JD` (correlation `prov-2c98a0a3`) -> Bootstrapping failed

Miles Thornton: The error surfaced to operators is basically: `BOOTSTRAP_FAILED: helm apply unsuccessful` with no actionable next step.

Miles Thornton: Can we please (1) tighten error classification for bootstrap failures, and (2) update runbook with a clear “if you see X, do Y” checklist? Right now it’s a lot of spelunking across logs.

provisioning-bot: Provisioning run update: pool=ded-az1-stg-015 run=prun_01HQR9P0M4 stage=Bootstrapping status=FAILED duration=52m
Summary: helm chart apply exceeded timeout
Links: logs=https://logs.redwood.ai/?q=prov-5a11d1f7 dashboard=https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ded-readiness?var-run=prun_01HQR9P0M4 runbook=https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/Dedicated+Pool+Provisioning+Runbook

Rafael Mendes: +1, saw the same pattern when I was shadowing earlier. Oncall can’t tell “helm values invalid” vs “cluster not reachable” vs “dns/tls” vs “kube-api throttling” from the top-level error.

Rafael Mendes: Miles can you paste one log excerpt that’s representative? (redact secrets)

Miles Thornton: Yup, from `prov-6f3c3b2a`:
```
level=error component=bootstrapper msg="helm upgrade failed" err="UPGRADE FAILED: failed to create resource: Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook \"validate.nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io\": Post https://ingress-nginx-controller-admission.ingress-nginx.svc:443/networking/v1/ingresses?timeout=10s: dial tcp: lookup ingress-nginx-controller-admission.ingress-nginx.svc on 10.96.0.10:53: no such host"
level=error component=bootstrapper msg="bootstrap step failed" step="helm_apply" retryable=true
level=warn  component=bootstrapper msg="retrying" attempt=3 backoff=120s
level=error component=bootstrapper msg="bootstrap aborted" err="context deadline exceeded"
```

Miles Thornton: Looks like kube-dns not ready / service discovery failing, but the operator sees only “helm apply timeout”.

Gabe Wilson: That’s super helpful. The classification is currently too coarse, agreed. We can emit a more specific failure code when we see common strings (e.g. `no such host` + `*.svc` => `BOOTSTRAP_DNS`), and include “check CoreDNS + cluster DNS health” in the operator message.

Victor Alvarez: On the networking side, we should treat that as “cluster DNS not functional yet” vs external DNS. The runbook should explicitly say:
- `kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=kube-dns`
- `kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/coredns --tail=50`
- quick check pod `nslookup kubernetes.default`

Victor Alvarez: Also we should confirm the bootstrapper waits for CoreDNS readiness before starting helm applies. Is it doing that? (I think not)

Gabe Wilson: It waits for API server + nodes ready, but not for DNS. We can add a lightweight preflight in Bootstrapping: create an ephemeral pod and `nslookup` a service name, fail fast with a clean error if it doesn’t resolve within N sec.

Rafael Mendes: That would reduce the “helm retries until timeout” behavior and get to a deterministic message.

Kira Thompson: Re runbook: I can add a dedicated Bootstrapping section with “symptoms -> checks -> remediation” if y’all tell me the top 5 classes we want.

Miles Thornton: Top ones we’ve seen in oncall notes:
1) DNS/service discovery inside cluster (like above)
2) webhook/admission failures (often just symptom of DNS)
3) `ImagePullBackOff` for bootstrap components (registry auth / mirror)
4) Helm values schema mismatch (bad config / invalid type)
5) kube-api throttling / `context deadline exceeded` while cluster is underprovisioned

Benji Okafor: For (4), we can hook config validation earlier (Validating) to catch the obvious values type issues before we even create the cluster. But some are runtime-only.

Benji Okafor: Can you share an example of a values schema mismatch error? If it’s coming from our chart templates we can detect `cannot unmarshal` etc.

Miles Thornton: Example from `prov-2c98a0a3` (eu1):
```
Error: UPGRADE FAILED: cannot patch "redwood-runtime" with kind Deployment:
json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field EnvVar.spec.template.spec.containers.env.value of type int64
```

Gabe Wilson: That one is 100% classifiable (`BOOTSTRAP_HELM_VALUES_TYPE`). Also should print which key was wrong (if we can surface from diff).

Rafael Mendes: Action items proposal:
- Gabe: add bootstrap preflight checks + error categorization + operator-facing hints
- Victor: provide DNS readiness checks content + confirm preflight commands
- Benji: add a validation rule / lint for common env var numeric/string mismatches if possible
- Kira: update runbook section + add links from error messages to anchors in the runbook

Kira Thompson: Works for me. Please send me the canonical doc link you want updated. Is it this runbook? https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/Dedicated+Pool+Provisioning+Runbook

Miles Thornton: Yep that’s the one oncall is using. Also would be great if error messages include the *exact* stage + a short remediation, like:
`BOOTSTRAPPING: DNS check failed (CoreDNS not ready). See runbook: ...#bootstrapping-dns`

Gabe Wilson: :thumbsup: I’ll take this. I’ll also update the bootstrapper to emit `failure_category` as a label in the provisioning event so dashboards can group by cause instead of just stage.

Rafael Mendes: Please also ensure the classification doesn’t explode cardinality (keep it to a small enum). We can agree on a handful:
- BOOTSTRAP_DNS
- BOOTSTRAP_IMAGE_PULL
- BOOTSTRAP_HELM_VALUES
- BOOTSTRAP_KUBE_API_TIMEOUT
- BOOTSTRAP_UNKNOWN

Gabe Wilson: Yep, that’s the intent.

Miles Thornton: Thanks. For immediate oncall mitigation: should we be advising folks to re-run Bootstrapping vs pause and debug? The CLI currently suggests “re-run stage”.

Rafael Mendes: If it’s DNS not ready, re-run is fine after verifying CoreDNS is up. If it’s values mismatch, re-run will just fail again until config fixed.

Kira Thompson: I’ll add that decision tree explicitly (rerun ok vs needs config change vs escalate).

Victor Alvarez: One more: sometimes DNS fails because CNI isn’t healthy yet. Add quick `kubectl -n kube-system get ds | grep -E 'cilium|calico'` and confirm pods Running.

Gabe Wilson: Good call. I’ll incorporate that in hints.

Miles Thornton: Cool. Please tag me on the PR so I can sanity-check it from oncall POV.

Gabe Wilson: Will do. Targeting EOD tomorrow for first pass.

Rafael Mendes: Also: let’s make sure the top-level error in the Slack bot message includes the category + 1-line hint. That’s what oncall sees first.

provisioning-bot: FYI: Additional context available for prun_01HQR7K8Z2
Last error category: unknown (legacy)
Next retry scheduled: none (max retries reached)

Miles Thornton: ^ this is exactly the pain. Looking forward to the category showing up.

Kira Thompson: I’ll start drafting the runbook changes now and leave TODO placeholders for the categories until Gabe lands them.

Rafael Mendes: Thanks all. Let’s keep this thread updated as PRs go out so oncall knows when behavior changes.
